summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of post-polio syndrome, osteoporosis, and coronary artery disease was admitted for acute worsening of chronic lower back pain and new bilateral great toe numbness. MRI revealed acute to subacute compression fractures at L3 and L5, an acute on chronic fracture at L2, and a severe chronic L1 fracture with spinal canal narrowing. Neurology and neurosurgery recommended conservative management with a TLSO brace, pain control, and rehabilitation. She was started on iron for low ferritin contributing to restless legs and continued on home medications for CAD and hypothyroidism. Urinary symptoms were chronic and not infectious. She was discharged to extended care for inpatient rehabilitation with follow-up planned in spine and cardiology clinics.
